description: The qmb data generate synthetic-generation capability is exposed on the CLI door (doors/cli/tree.py adapts qmb.data.generate and DATA_COMMANDS includes 'generate') but is ABSENT from the Python API door (qmb.doors.api re-exports download/verify/gap_check/list_data/catalog but not generate; no api.generate attribute). The shipped parity catalog doors/parity.py CAPABILITY_LIBRARY maps data.generate -> (DATA_COMMANDS, data_front_identity), omitting the generate library fn, so the door-parity contract does not catch the gap. Jointly confirmed by Epic 16 F16-F02.
expected: B-1 door parity: the generate library capability reachable identically from BOTH the CLI door and the Python API door.
observed: generate is reachable from the CLI door but absent from the Python API door surface; an in-process API/UI caller cannot generate synthetic series the CLI can. FAIL confirmed against current source; the pin locks parity post-repair.

description: A history-seeded generator ignores the cited source dataset's declared scale: the draw adapters (e.g. _draw_block_bootstrap/_draw_gaussian_*) compute on the source bars' raw integers and use config.scale for the money-path crossing, never reading the source bars' own declared scale. A source declared at scale 3 fed to a target instrument at scale 5 yields synthetic prices in the SOURCE integer magnitude (~1201) reinterpreted at scale 5 — a 100x mis-scaling — with no named AD-7/AD-22 conversion and no refusal.
expected: Prices quantized to the target instrument tick via the named AD-7/AD-22 conversion (lineage-carrying, declared rounding), OR a typed invalid input refusal for a scale-incompatible source (DEC-0105: conversions derived with lineage, never a silent rescale).
observed: generate() returns Ok with closes [1201,1202,1203,1204,1205] at scale 5 (source magnitude reused verbatim) — neither target-scale-converted (~120000) nor refused. FAIL confirmed against current source.

description: The B-7 replay-clock-vs-provenance guard in resolve_generator_config (_refuse_replay_clock_on_synthetic) fires at the flat top level but is EVADED when the generator config is nested under a 'generator_config' key: the nested-config merge carries forward only destination/output_root/calendar/source_series and DROPS an outer-level clock/world directive before the guard runs, so a composed config with clock=replay (or world=live) wrapping a synthetic generator config resolves Ok instead of refusing. Highest severity: re-opens the synthetic-on-money-path backdoor B-7 closes.
expected: Config compilation RETURNS a typed invalid input for a replay clock (or non-simulated world) bound to synthetic-tainted data, identical to the flat case; the guard must check every nested/composed binding, not just the root (B-7 wins over B-2).
observed: Flat clock=replay refuses (invalid input, field=clock); nested {generator_config, clock=replay} and {generator_config, world=live} both resolve Ok with no refusal. FAIL confirmed against current source.
